subtype: Refusing a huge favour, then feeling bound by a smaller one [Receiver]
passage: Tanvir, you said yes to the society's "small favour" right after refusing the big one? Sit, and let your Sudha Phuphi tell you something. When I was twenty, our hostel senior asked me to run the entire annual fest. Every committee, every sponsor. I said no, firmly, and I was proud of myself. Then she sighed, looked hurt and said, "Fine, you're right, it's too much. Could you at least handle the food stalls?" I heard myself say yes before she had finished. She had given something up, so I felt I had to give something back. The food stalls meant three weeks of phone calls and one burnt tent. I never wanted the food stalls either. If she had asked me that first, I would have said no in one breath.

qa.q: What did the senior first ask Sudha to run?
qa.a: The entire annual fest.

qa.q: Why did young Sudha say yes to the food stalls before the senior finished?
qa.a: She felt guilty after refusing, because the senior had given something up and looked hurt, so a yes seemed owed in return.

qa.q: What question could young Sudha have asked before agreeing to the food stalls?
qa.a: Whether she would have agreed to the food stalls if that had been the first request; her own answer, no in one breath, would have freed her.

qa.q: Why might Phuphi be telling Tanvir this story now?
qa.a: Tanvir has just agreed to a "small favour" after refusing a big one, and Phuphi wants Tanvir to recognise the same pull she felt at twenty.

grounding: An aunt recalls how, at twenty, turning down a huge request made her feel bound to accept the smaller one that followed.

subtype: Refusing a huge favour, then feeling bound by a smaller one [Receiver]
passage: It was 9:55 p.m., the hostel gate closed at ten, and Abhinav was blocking the corridor. "Yusuf, lend me your scooter for the Goa trip. Just ten days." "No way. I need it for my internship." Abhinav's shoulders dropped. "Okay, okay, too much, you're right." Then, quickly: "Then just let me use it every evening this week. Only that." The warden's whistle blew. Yusuf felt a strange tug. Abhinav had backed down; it felt rude not to meet him halfway. "Fine, I guess," he started. Then he stopped. Would he have said yes if every evening this week had been the first ask? He needed those evenings for his project. "Actually, no. One evening. Thursday." He ran for the gate.

qa.q: When did the hostel gate close?
qa.a: At ten.

qa.q: What was the "strange tug" Yusuf felt?
qa.a: After Abhinav backed down from the big request, Yusuf felt he ought to meet him halfway and agree to the smaller one, as if he owed it.

qa.q: What choice did Yusuf make before running for the gate, and why was it sound?
qa.a: He asked whether he would agree to every evening as a first request, saw he needed those evenings for his project, and offered only Thursday.

qa.q: How might the asking look from Abhinav's side?
qa.a: Abhinav may truly need the scooter and not be planning any trick; backing down and asking for less may simply feel reasonable to him.

grounding: Under time pressure, a young man who refused a big request feels bound to accept the smaller compromise that follows, before checking it on its own.

subtype: Refusing a huge favour, then feeling bound by a smaller one [Receiver]
passage: In Rashmi's one-room flat in Lajpat Nagar, her phone buzzed. Her cousin Yash. "Rashmi, can six of my friends stay at your place during my wedding week? Please?" She looked at her single mattress and her exam timetable. "Yash, no. I'm sorry. My exams are that week." A long pause. Then: "Totally understand. Too much. Okay, then can I at least keep their luggage at yours for the month? Only eight bags." Eight bags would cover the whole floor. Rashmi's thumb moved toward "ok" anyway. He had accepted her no so nicely. Wasn't it her turn to give something? She sat on the mattress, the phone warm in her hand, feeling guilty and cornered at once.

qa.q: How many bags did Yash want to keep at Rashmi's flat?
qa.a: Eight bags.

qa.q: What was Rashmi feeling as her thumb moved toward "ok"?
qa.a: She felt guilty and cornered at once; because Yash accepted her no so nicely, she felt she owed him a yes, even though the bags would cover her floor.

qa.q: What could Rashmi ask herself before replying?
qa.a: Whether she would agree to eight bags for a month if that had been Yash's first request; if not, she can kindly say no to this too.

qa.q: How might Yash see the luggage request?
qa.a: Yash may think it's a small, fair compromise after the big no, without noticing it would fill Rashmi's floor during her exams.

grounding: After refusing a cousin's big request, a young woman feels an urge to accept the smaller compromise, as if it is now her turn to give.

subtype: Refusing a huge favour, then feeling bound by a smaller one [Receiver]
passage:
'Darshan, bro, one huge favour. Write my whole project report? You're so good at it.'
'Madhav, no. It's forty pages. I have my own report.'
'Yeah, yeah. Too much. Sorry, I shouldn't have asked.'
'It's fine.'
Madhav stirred his tea in the canteen, looking at the table. 'You're right. Totally. Okay... then could you just make the slides? Only the slides. Twelve, max.'
Darshan opened his mouth to say no again. But Madhav had backed down so quickly, and he looked so tired.
'Twelve slides?'
'Max. Please, yaar. I'll buy you samosas all week.'
'...Fine. Send me the data.'
'You're the best!'
Madhav left. Darshan sat alone, looking at his own half-done report. Twelve slides was still two nights' work. Why had he said yes? He had just refused something bigger. Somehow that had made this feel like his turn to give.

qa.q: How many slides did Madhav ask Darshan to make?
qa.a: He asked for the slides only, twelve, max.

qa.q: Why did Darshan find it hard to say no to the slides?
qa.a: Madhav had backed down so quickly from the big request that it felt like Madhav had given way, so Darshan felt it was his turn to give, and he cared about his tired friend.

qa.q: What could Darshan have asked himself before saying 'Fine'?
qa.a: He could have asked whether he would agree to two nights of slides if that had been the first request, given his own half-done report.

qa.q: How might Madhav see the conversation?
qa.a: Madhav probably feels relieved and grateful, and may not realise how much work he has passed on to Darshan.

grounding: A young man refuses to write his friend's whole report, then feels pulled into making the slides, as if the friend's backing down meant it was his turn to give.

subtype: Refusing a huge favour, then feeling bound by a smaller one [Receiver]
passage: Last winter my cousin Asif called me late one night. I'm Irawati, and Asif and I grew up in the same house, so I love him like a brother. He asked me to lend him fifty thousand rupees for a bike. Fifty thousand! I had just started my first job. I said no, as gently as I could. He went quiet and then said, 'You're right. That was too much. I'm sorry, Ira Didi.' I felt bad hearing him sound so small. Then he said, 'Could you just lend me five thousand for the down payment? Only that.' And I said yes almost before he finished. It felt like he had given something up for me, and now I should give something back. Looking back, five thousand was a lot for me then too. If he had asked for it first, I'd have thought about it for a week. I don't regret helping him. I just wish I'd noticed why I said yes.

qa.q: How much did Asif first ask Irawati to lend him?
qa.a: He first asked her to lend him fifty thousand rupees for a bike.

qa.q: Why did Irawati say yes to the five thousand so quickly?
qa.a: She loved Asif and felt bad hearing him sound small, and it felt like he had given something up, so she should give something back.

qa.q: What could Irawati do next time someone follows a refused big request with a smaller one?
qa.a: She could pause and ask whether she'd agree if the smaller request had come first, and take time to think instead of answering at once.

qa.q: How might Asif have felt after Irawati agreed to the smaller loan?
qa.a: Asif was probably relieved and grateful, perhaps not noticing that the big-then-small ask made it hard for her to refuse.

grounding: A young woman looks back on refusing a cousin's large loan and then agreeing at once to a smaller one, feeling it was her turn after he backed down.
